title: IT WAS THE LORD WHO FOUGHT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You yourselves have seen everything the Lord your God has done to all these nations for your sake; it was the Lord your God who fought for you. Remember how I have allotted as an inheritance for your tribes all the land of the nations that remain — the nations I conquered — between the Jordan and the Mediterranean Sea in the west. The Lord your God himself will push them out for your sake. He will drive them out before you, and you will take possession of their land, as the Lord your God promised you." — Josh 23:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Joshua begins his charge, he does not start with commands. He starts with what God has done. "It was the Lord your God who fought for you." The victories Israel enjoyed were not the achievements of clever generals or brave soldiers; they were the gift of God fighting on their behalf.

This is the right foundation for any call to obedience — remembering grace first. Before Joshua asks anything of the people, he reminds them of everything God has already given. Gratitude, not guilt, is meant to be the engine of a faithful life.

Notice too that some of the work still lay ahead: "The Lord your God himself will push them out for your sake." God had done much and would do more. Israel's part was to trust and press forward; God's part was to give the victory.

This is a beautiful picture of how we live the Christian life. We are not left to fight our battles alone. The same God who has already saved us continues to work in us and for us. Our great victory over sin and death was won not by our strength but by Christ (1 Cor 15:57). When you face the battles that remain, remember: the Lord your God fights for you. Move forward in trust, resting on the One who has never lost.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you remember God's past faithfulness when facing new battles?
2. How does knowing "the Lord fights for you" change your outlook?
3. What victory are you trying to win in your own strength instead of His?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You have fought for me and still do. Help me to remember Your grace and to face every battle trusting in Your strength, not my own. Amen.
